title: Finite constant coefficients in proper smooth curve families
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]) and $f:C\to S$ a proper smooth morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with nonempty geometrically connected fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] of dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $M$ a finite $\Lambda$-module. For every integer $q$, $R^qf_*\underline M$ is a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. No invertibility of the additive exponent of $M$ on $S$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use Scheme.isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf from the proved source module ConstructibleEtaleModuleSheafComparison to translate the finite-value predicate to source constructibility. Apply homology to rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility to compare bounded-below and total derived direct images. These comparisons change neither coefficients nor degree.

For a nonempty smooth connected scheme over a field, regularity makes it integral. A smooth chart has some relative dimension n, and a nonempty open of an integral scheme has the same dimension as the scheme. Thus the scheme is smooth of relative dimension n everywhere. Apply this to each residue-field fibre and its algebraic-closure base change: smooth relative dimension is stable under base change and equals topological Krull dimension. The geometric and ordinary fibre dimensions therefore agree. Apply the stated dimension-loci theorem with d=1 to obtain the open and closed zero- and one-dimensional loci, including empty loci.

On the zero-dimensional locus, the open singleton property from the dimension-loci theorem gives discrete fibres, hence a locally quasi-finite morphism. Properness makes it finite. In degree zero use higherDirectImage_zero_constant_constructible. In every nonzero integer degree use the proved source theorem isZero_homology_rightDerivedLowerStar_singleFunctor_of_isFinite from ConstructibleSheaf.FiniteDerived, which follows from exactness of finite direct image. Zero sheaves are constructible.

On the one-dimensional locus use the already proved, invertibility-free source APIs isConstructibleSheaf_homology_constantSheaf_restrictScalars_iff and constructibleHomology_rightDerivedLowerStar_constantSheaf_zmod in Finiteness.CoefficientDevissage. The characteristic N of a finite ring R is nonzero. The canonical map ULift(ZMod N) to R restricts M to a finite ZMod N module and preserves and reflects constructibility of its constant higher direct images. The source devissage theorem inducts on the cardinality of that finite module, using a cyclic prime-order submodule and the strictly smaller quotient. Its inputs are constructibility for every prime p dividing N and every integer degree. For nonnegative degrees supply properSmoothCurves_prime_higherDirectImage_constructible and the bounded-below/total comparison. For negative degrees the right-derived image of a degree-zero sheaf lies in degrees at least zero, so homology vanishes. N=1 and the zero module are included in the source cardinality induction. No invertibility hypothesis is used.

Restriction to either open locus commutes with higher direct images by the proved source upperStarHomologyRightDerivedLowerStarIso from Finiteness.TargetLocal. Scheme.upperStarConstantSheafIso identifies the restricted input with the constant sheaf. Transfer the constructibility just proved along this isomorphism and glue with the proved source Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf.of_iSup_eq_top from ConstructibleSheaf.OpenCover. Convert back to the unchanged finite-value module-sheaf predicate. All source APIs named here are existing proved declarations; no additional statement is introduced.
